minutes_text:
Inglewood, California
  March 4, 2025

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  March 4, 2025, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
  Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance
  Authority, Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at the hour of 2:02 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Finance
  Authority Secretary/Parking Authority Secretary/Joint Powers Authority Secretary
  announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman/Parking Authority
  Chairman/Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts,
  Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members/Finance Authority Members/Parking
  Authority Members/Joint Powers Authority Members
  Padilla, Morales, Faulk; and
  Absent:  Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members/Finance Authority Members/Parking
  Authority Members/Joint Powers Authority Members
  Gray.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/ officials and personnel
  present were as follows:
  Aisha L Thompson  City Clerk/ Secretary*
  Louis A. Atwell  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Rick R. Olivarez  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Destinee Wesley  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority Members on
  any item on the Agendas.

  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT WARRANTS AND BILLS – RECEIVED AND FILED. The demands
  presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated February 13,
  2025, in the amount of $7,059,574.83 is hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor
  Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said
  registers that said demand is received and filed.

  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts ordered the
  Warrants and Bills received and filed.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Padilla that the Minutes for the City Council Meetings held on January 28, 2025, and
  February 4, 2025, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.
 March 4, 2025

183  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 25-134 APPROVED –
  NATIONAL POOLS INC., DBA NPI CONCRETE; CITY CONTROLLED AND
  DIRECTED FIFTEEN PERCENT (15%) PROJECT CONTINGENCY –
  APPROVED; RESOLUTION NO. 25-53 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE FISCAL
  YEAR 2024-2025 OPERATING BUDGET. Staff report dated March 4, 2025, was
  presented recommending the Mayor and Council Members award a contract and approve
  an agreement with National Pools Inc., dba NPI Concrete, for the Vincent Park Swimming
  Pool Deck Improvement Project, per Bid No. CB-25-02.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Award contract and approve agreement No. 25-134 not to
  exceed $200,000; 2) Approve an additional City-controlled and directed 15% contingency,
  not to exceed $30,000, for a total amount of $230,000, per Bid No. CB-25-02; and 3) Adopt
  Resolution No. 25-53 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION FOR THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2024-25 TO FUND AN
  AGREEMENT WITH NATIONAL POOLS INC. FOR THE VINCENT
  PARK SWIMMING POOL DECK IMPROVEMENT PROJECT

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

183  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 25-135 APPROVED – JCI
  JONES CHEMICALS, INC. Staff report dated March 4, 2025, was presented
  recommending the Mayor and Council Members award a contract and approve an
  agreement with JCI Jones Chemicals, Inc., for Supply and Delivery of Liquid Chlorine, per
  Bid No. RFB-0186.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby award contract and approve agreement No. 25-135 not to
  exceed $385,468. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

183  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 25-136 APPROVED –
  WOODARD & CURRAN, INC.; CITY CONTROLLED AND DIRECTED TEN
  PERCENT (10%) PROJECT CONTINGENCY – APPROVED. Staff report dated
  March 4, 2025, was presented recommending the Mayor and Council Members award a
  contract and approve an agreement with Woodward & Curran, Inc., for the Stormwater
  Prioritization Study, per RFP No. 0236.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Award contract and approve Agreement No. 25-136___
  not to exceed $149,878; and 2) Authorize an additional City-controlled and directed ten
  percent (10%) contingency not to exceed $14,988. The motion was carried by the following
  roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

  2
 March 4, 2025

183  AMENDMENT NO. 3 TO AGREEMENT NO. 20-265 APPROVED – HF&H
  CONSULTANTS, LLC; RESOLUTION NO. 25-53 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE
  FISCAL YEAR OPERATING BUDGET. Staff report dated March 4, 2025, was
  presented recommending the Mayor and Council Members approve Amendment No. 3 to
  Agreement No. 20-265 with HF&H Consultants, LLC to amend the scope of services and
  increase the amount by $180,000, for a total contract amount not to exceed $479,000, over
  the current term of three (3) years.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Amendment No. 3 to Agreement No. 20-265;
  and 2) Adopt Resolution No. 25-54 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION FOR THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2024-25 TO FUND AN
  ADDITION TO THE SCOPE OF SERVICES FOR THE AGREEMENT WITH
  HF&F CONSULTANTS, LLC

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

183  AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO AGREEMENT NO. 22-155 APPROVED –HNTB
  CORPORATION. Staff report dated March 4, 2025, was presented recommending the
  Mayor and Council Members approve Amendment No.1 to Agreement No. 22-155 with
  NHTB Corporation to exercise the City’s option to extend the agreement for an additional
  year to continue providing on-call professional project administrative support services, with
  no increase in funding.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby Approve Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 22-155.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

131.8  EXCLUSIVE NEGOTIATION AGREEMENT NOS. 25-137, 25-138 AND 25-139 –
  APPROVED – HABITAT FOR HUMANITY OF GREATER LOS ANGELES. -Staff
  report dated March 4, 2025, was presented recommending the Mayor and Council Members
  approve agreement Nos. 3 with Habitat for Humanity of Greater Los Angeles., a California
  nonprofit public benefit corporation, for the following Housing Asset Parcels, collectively,
  (Project(s)”0:
  1. 8244 Crenshaw Drive and 8205 Crenshaw Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90305
  2. 958 Orchard Drive Inglewood, CA 90301: and
  3. 708 W. Beach Avenue Inglewood, CA 90302.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve exclusive negotiation Agreement Nos. 25-137, 25-
  138 and 25-139. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

183  PUBLIC HEARING SET – ENERGY EFFICIENCY AND RENEWABLE ENERGY
  PROJECT. Staff report dated March 4, 2025, was presented requesting a public hearing
  to be set for the Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy Project., pursuant to California
  Government code 4217.

  Mayor Butts set the Public Hearing for March 25, 2025, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.

  3
 March 4, 2025

301  ORDINANCE NO. 25-07 ADOPTED – APPROVING ZONING CODE
  AMENDMENT NO. 24-00003 (ZCA-00003). Staff report dated March 4, 2025, was
  presented recommending the Mayor and Council Members adopt Ordinance No. 25-07,
  approving Zoning Code Amendment No. 24-00003 (ZCA-00003) to extent the hours of the
  on-site sale of alcohol until 4:00 AM in the Sports and Entertainment (SE) Overlay Zone.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

  Thereupon, it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that
  Ordinance No. 25-07 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEOOD, CALIFORNIA, TO APPROVE ZONING CODE
  AMENDMENT ZCA-24-00003 TO EXTEND THE HOURS OF THE ON-
  SITE SALE OF ALCOHOL UNTIL 4:00 A.M. IN THE SPORTS AND
  ENTERTAINMENT(SE) OVERLAY ZONE.

  which was introduced at the meeting held on February 25, 2025, be adopted. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Gray.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished
  to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not elsewhere
  considered on the Agenda.

  Susana Sanchez, the sister of Juan Sanchez, spoke out about the tragic loss of her brother,
  who was murdered in Inglewood. She described Juan as a hardworking family man with a
  deep love for helping others. Susana emphasized that her brother was not only a devoted
  member of his family but also a proud Inglewood resident who always sought to make a
  positive impact in his community.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in the memory of Juan Sanchez and June Chavez at the hour of 2:24 p.m.

  Approved this 15th day of April, 2025.
  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
